drafted_from: tool:look-at-screen row in tools/look-at-screen/tool-rows.json, do-work/look-at-screen.mjs, read-data/rules.json and test/look-at-screen.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Look at my screen now and tell me what is on it; make the pictures at most 800 pixels on the long side and include the mouse pointer." It runs tool:look-at-screen once and describes each display.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it takes a picture only when run, keeps nothing on the Mac and answers the pictures in its reply.
instructions: 1. Allow Screen Recording for the app that runs the tool in System Settings, Privacy & Security; without it the tool answers needs_access and captures nothing.

2. Say "Look at my screen"; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:look-at-screen, with long_edge (200 to 1600 pixels) and cursor (true to show the pointer) if you want them.

3. Read the answer: pictures has one entry per display, the main one first, each with display, main, width and height in pixels, media_type image/jpeg and base64 bytes; use the pixel sizes to point at an exact spot.
4. If the answer says the displays are too many for one answer, disconnect some or ask again; nothing is kept on the Mac either way.

worked_examples.title: Two displays, main first, pointer on
worked_examples.ask: Look at my screen now, small pictures, with the pointer.
worked_examples.given: From tools/look-at-screen/test/look-at-screen.test.mjs (system commands stood in for): a Mac with two displays, Screen Recording allowed, the first picture 1600 by 900 and the second 1200 by 750 after shrinking. Read from do-work/look-at-screen.mjs: long_edge 800 is under the rules' limit of 1600 so it is used, and cursor true is passed to the capture.
worked_examples.hands_back: pictures: [{display 1, main true, width 1600, height 900, media_type "image/jpeg", base64 ...}, {display 2, main false, width 1200, height 750, media_type "image/jpeg", base64 ...}] (sizes as the shrink step reports them), said "This is what is on the screen now, the main display first; each picture gives its size in pixels." and looked_at a time. With Screen Recording off it answers {needs_access: "screen-recording", said: "Turn on Screen Recording for the app that runs this tool in System Settings, Privacy & Security, so it can see your screen when you ask."} and captures nothing.
